newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurers plan campaign against tax plans.
newsitem.headline: German insurers plan campaign against tax plans.

text.p: German insurers on Tuesday vowed to mobilise their customers and parliamentarians to protest against government plans to slap a 10 percent tax on life insurance returns.
The tax plans are part of a sweeping reform of the German taxation system revealed last week in Bonn, which insurers claim will cut returns on up to 80 million contracts.

"The final word has not yet been spoken on this matter," said Bernd Michaels, president of Germany's GDV insurance association, as he announced the group's forthcoming protest advertising campaign over the tax plans.
The GDV is planning to place ads in daily newspapers from Friday as well as mail all customers to inform them of the added cost. An open letter has already been sent to parliamentary delegates.

The GDV's life insurance expert Gerhard Rupprecht, also chief executive of Germany's biggest life insurer Allianz Leben, said holders of standard 35-year policies could expect to lose about 15 percent of their returns because of the levy.

Michaels warned that the tax plans could dissuade customers from providing for themselves in their old age, creating holes which the state would be forced to try to fill, or that more Germans might invest their money abroad.
The fact that the tax plans would also affect existing policies would unnerve clients, he said, making them dubious about the validity of policy conditions.
